$comment: Formatter families. A family describes what stays the same across its versions; the version is chosen per run (family@version) and installed into tools/<family>@<version>/ by `pnpm arena tool add`. Fields: package: the npm package installed, or release: a GitHub release the binary comes from (repo, tag with {version}, and the asset per <platform>-<arch> with the executable's path inside it), whose sha256 per platform is recorded in tools/<id>/release.json when the version is added; with: companion packages pinned at one exact version for every version of the family (dprint's language plugins); versions: the major versions this family covers; binary: per <platform>-<arch>, or '*' for every platform, the package holding the executable and its path inside it (a missing platform means no build is published for it); runtime: 'node' when the executable is a JavaScript file run with the current node; languages: the languages it formats, of those in src/lib/languages.ts; notes: how it formats a language, shown in the site's Languages dialog; asHtml: languages it formats with another language's parser (Angular templates as plain HTML), so its output there is not that language's; check: the arguments that report unformatted files without writing; checkDiffers: the exit code check mode uses when some file would change (dprint uses 20, the others 1); write: the arguments that format in place; {config} is the arena's generated config, written outside the staged files; env: environment for every invocation, where {cache} is a folder kept with the tool (dprint compiles its plugins there once); threads: thread settings as documented, as flags ({one}, {n}) or environment variables ({env}), {n} replaced, or null when it documents none; defaultThreads: what it uses with no setting, as documented; keep: how many versions the store keeps, newest first (default 3); about: who maintains it and why the arena tests it, shown in the site's Libs dialog; source: where the thread settings are documented.

families.name: prettier
families.description: The JavaScript code formatter, the reference

about.why: The formatter most projects run today, and the output every other formatter here aims to match.

notes.angular: Its angular parser, set for .html files by an override

families.source: Prettier's CLI formats one file after another and documents no thread option

families.name: bun
families.description: Bun's built-in formatter (bun fmt), written in Rust

about.why: A formatter inside a runtime that reads Prettier's config and aims at Prettier's output.

notes.angular: Prettier's angular parser setting, read from the same override

families.source: bun fmt --help --all: --threads, default one per CPU core

families.name: oxfmt
families.description: The Oxc project's formatter, written in Rust

about.language: Rust, shipped as a Node native addon
about.why: A Prettier compatible formatter from the team behind oxlint, reading Prettier's option names.

notes.angular: Its angular-html language, set for .html files by an association

families.name: biome
families.description: Biome's formatter (biome format), written in Rust

about.why: A formatter and linter in one native binary, aiming at Prettier's output for the languages it formats.

notes.angular: No Angular template parser in this release: control flow (@if, @for, @let) stays text

families.source: biome format --help documents no thread option; BIOME_THREADS is documented for biome ci only

families.name: dprint
families.description: dprint with its TypeScript, JSON, Markdown, Malva (CSS), YAML and markup (HTML) plugins, written in Rust

about.why: A pluggable formatter with its own style, not Prettier's: it shows how far another style is, at native speed.

notes.angular: Angular mode for files named .component.html, which the arena stages every template as; dprint's own style

families.name: tidy
families.description: A single Rust binary that prints what Prettier prints

about.why: Ports Prettier's printers and claims byte for byte agreement with Prettier 3.9.9 on its own corpus.

notes.angular: No Angular parser (--lang angular is refused): templates are formatted as HTML
